context: Wilde to Frank Harris, [circa 20 September 1900], Paris. The settlement that the October quarrel is about: Harris had proposed collaborating and then arrived with the play already written, so Wilde proposes to sell him the plot outright and sets out the terms. Six days later he signs the assignment; three weeks later Harris pays £25 of the £175.
quote:
Dear Frank — Our misunderstanding of last night came from the fact that you had proposed collaboration, and then appeared with the play finished. I have not seen a line of it, and now I think — and I dare say you will also — that there is no necessity I should — So let the matter be concluded in this way.

You buy my plot and scenario — for the terms you proposed last night.

£200 down.
£500 shares in the Reserve
1/4 of profits of play —

I will send Bellew his money — and of course he has no claim on you of any kind —

Will you send me a line to corroborate this — or, better still, come and see me, or make an appointment for dinner.

I am writing in bed — in considerable pain —

Ever Oscar
original_provenance: Read at HRC 2676, images 48-49 - one bifolium: image 48 shows sides 4 (left) and 1 (right), image 49 the inner opening, sides 2 and 3. Emphasis: none, a null finding, and no dateline to underline - this is one of the few he left undated, which is why the volume dates it '[Circa 20 September 1900]'. Another hand, and not A kind one: '**Blackmailer**' is written down the left margin of side 4, vertically, in ink, in a firm upright hand that is not Wilde's - beside the letter in which he asks Harris to buy the plot. Confirmed at 5x, rotated. Whose hand it is I cannot say and have not guessed; Harris, a later owner and a dealer are all possible. The volume records nothing of it. It is worth knowing that somebody read this letter as an extortion and wrote so on it. Read with care: 'for the terms you proposed' reads as 'on the terms' at page size and is 'for' at 4.5x - his f carries the descender loop. The volume is right. OCR Warning: our text mirror renders one line of this letter as reversed gibberish ('ue yo nok uo u ou sy ay ssno yo pue auo s mg puss m 1'). The printed page reads 'I will send Bellew his money, and of course he has no claim on you of any kind.' Recovered by rendering p. 1198 from the PDF, not from the mirror.
